title: A view takes arguments from the command line and the bus
intention: cairn <device> show|get <view> --key value ... passes the pairs to the view as keyword arguments, over the bus, so any read a device offers is reachable from the command line: show renders it for a human, get returns JSON for a machine.
why: Akien 2026-10-13: "cairn's intention is to be the command line access to the bus" and "it would be: cairn inference_domain show/get calls --limit 20 --- show for me (formatted), get for you (json)". Measured 2026-10-13: cairn <device> show/get already resolves over the bus (shim.py cli_main -> RemoteBus().verbs), but a view is called with no arguments: shim.py _resolve calls device_views[name]() and device.py _handle_get/_handle_show call view_fn(). So a parameterised read (the inference calls, bounded by limit and since) cannot be a view, and b905340f8162 had to make it a bus verb the command line cannot reach ('no such verb calls').
traces_to: RULE 1 and the cairn command's intention as Akien stated it 2026-10-13 (the command line access to the bus: every read a device offers is reachable from a terminal through the device's public interface), and Law 1 (one resolver for every device instead of a script per read).
how: cairn/tools/base only. (a) shim.py _resolve: after the view name, parse the remaining tokens as --key value pairs (a bare --flag is value 'true'; a token not starting with -- is exit 2 naming it) into args (keys with - folded to _). (b) Check args against inspect.signature(view_fn): a key the view does not declare is exit 2, text 'cairn <dev>: view <name> takes no argument <key> — it takes: <params or (none)>'. (c) With args, call view_fn(**args) (values stay strings; the view coerces). A parameterised call is never answered from last_known: args imply hot (the device is woken as the hot modifier does). (d) device.py _handle_get/_handle_show read envelope body 'args' (dict, default {}), apply the same signature check (accepted False, reason naming the key and the params) and call view_fn(**args). No-argument calls are unchanged.
falsifier: cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_a_view_takes_arguments.py under PROVES {'35b92c5de7ef': {'1','2','3','4','5'}} over an inline device whose view echo(limit=None) returns {'limit': limit} and whose view bare() takes none: (1) shim resolve(['get','echo','--limit','3']) is exit 0 and its JSON data is {'limit': '3'}; (2) resolve(['show','echo','--limit','3']) is exit 0 and its text is _render_view('echo', {'limit': '3'}); (3) resolve(['get','echo','--bogus','1']) is exit 2 and the text names bogus and limit; (4) resolve(['get','bare','--limit','1']) is exit 2; (5) device._handle_get({'body': {'what': 'echo', 'args': {'limit': '3'}}}) returns accepted True with data {'limit': '3'}. Hollow: today's shim.py and device.py red 1, 2, 3 and 5.
watchme: none, because the fault is measured at /home/akien/dev/src/cairn/cairn/tools/base/shim.py and the proof's teeth are its falsifier
intent_berth: none, because Akien specified it in conversation 2026-10-13, his words recorded verbatim at /home/akien/dev/src/CairnCommons/ideas/2026-10-13-so-lets-talk-first-about-the-cairn.json and quoted in why

decisions.text: show is formatted for Akien, get is JSON for Claude, per Akien 2026-10-13 verbatim (in why). Arguments ride both identically.
Arguments are --key value strings and the view coerces: the resolver stays ignorant of each view's types, and a view's signature is its argument contract. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-12

A call with arguments is always hot: last_known holds one snapshot per view with no arguments, so answering a parameterised read from it would be a wrong answer presented as cached. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-12

The proof cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_a_view_takes_arguments.py is already written and committed before the build; the builder does NOT write or edit it. It drives the shim in a subprocess per command under a scratch HOME carrying a LIVE ground_loop liveness record, as test_root_verbs.py does. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-12 'approved thru PROVED'

device.py gains 'import inspect' and a module-level function view_args_refusal(name, view_fn, args) -> str | None: None when args is empty or the view takes **kwargs; otherwise the first key not among the view's POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD/KEYWORD_ONLY parameter names returns 'view <name> takes no argument <key> — it takes: <names space-joined, or (none)>'. shim.py imports it from cairn.tools.base.device, so both mouths share one check. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-12 'approved thru PROVED'

In _handle_get and _handle_show, after the 'no view' refusal: args = body.get('args') or {}; a non-dict args is refused accepted False with reason 'view <what> args must be a mapping, got <type>'; a view_args_refusal is refused accepted False with that reason; otherwise data = view_fn(**args). CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-12 'approved thru PROVED'

In shim.py _resolve, right after rest/hot are computed: for verb show or get with tokens after the view name, those tokens are parsed into args and removed from rest; a token not starting with '--' (or exactly '--') returns exit 2 'cairn <dev>: <tok> is not an argument — arguments are --key value'; then hot = True. Before the root/device_views dispatch, view_args_refusal over device_views[name] (a root view counts as taking none) returns exit 2 'cairn <dev>: <refusal>'; the call becomes device_views[name](**args). CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-12 'approved thru PROVED'

_resolve already picks root (status/settings) or device_views[name] before calling; the --key value parse runs for every show/get, and just before the existing 'if root is not None:' branch the check is view_args_refusal(name, (lambda: None) if root is not None else device_views[name], args) — so a root view is checked against a zero-parameter stand-in and refuses any argument (exit 2), while a device view is checked against its own signature and then called as device_views[name](**args). Root views' own code is unchanged. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-12 'approved thru PROVED'
decisions.step: D7a root views versus device views in _resolve
